identification.description: Climbing herb with rough quadrangular stems, whorled leaves and long reddish roots.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial climber or scrambling herb with rooting underground portions.
identification.root: Long cylindrical reddish-brown roots and rhizomatous portions; characteristic dye-producing material.
identification.stem: Slender, rough, angular and climbing with small hooks/prickles.
identification.leaf: Simple leaves often in whorls of four, ovate to lanceolate with rough surface.
identification.flower: Small greenish to yellowish flowers in branched clusters.
identification.fruit: Small globose berries, becoming dark on maturity.

therapeutics.precautions: Avoid converting the traditional 'Raktashodhana' term into an unsupported modern biomedical claim.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Indian madder is historically important as a natural dye and is also a traditional medicinal root; modern evidence should be evaluated by specific indication.
modern_information.safety_notes: Authentication is important because roots of unrelated species may be substituted.
